title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
domain: particle physics (jet tagging foundation model, infrared safety)

headline_result.text: On the small OmniLearned model, the selected Claude Opus 5.5 WSP edit (no gradients, at most 50 queries) restored W efficiency after a soft photon from 54% to 79% with remaining response 0.05, matching LoRA fine-tuning (0.06, 79%) while changing about 10,000 versus 63,240 parameters and keeping physical response at 1.01 versus 0.90.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3 runs per WSP variant and model size; 3 seeds for selected fine-tuning

key_claims.claim: WSP changed the rest of the model least: physical response within 1% of the original versus 0.90 for fine-tuning and 0.78 for the SAE edit, with about six times fewer parameters than fine-tuning.
key_claims.quote: WSP is the method that changes the rest of the model the least.

key_claims.claim: Run-to-run variation is the method's weak point: with the same prompt, remaining error differs by up to a factor of three and edit size from 142 to about 10,000 parameters.
key_claims.quote: The weak point of the method is the variation between runs.

notes_for_review: A careful non-LLM-target WSP study: the flaw is first located by mechanistic analysis, then repaired three ways (LoRA rank-8 fine-tuning with a hand-built loss, SAE-guided rank-one key edits, and Claude Opus 5.5 agents with 50 evaluation queries) and scored on held-out jets against an input removal rule. Controls include a random-latent SAE ablation, a frozen-random dictionary threshold, three runs per variant, prompts fixed and checksummed before launch, access logging, and a discard rule declared in advance (not a formal preregistration). WSP matches fine-tuning on the targeted repair with fewer changed parameters and better preservation of physical response, but needs target predictions to work well and varies strongly between runs; code, transcripts and weights are released (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.24377675).
